text: You're the new ServiceNow administrator for Lakeview Facilities, a 40-person department onboarding for the first time. This lesson and the next take them from zero to production-ready, using exactly what Chapters 1 through 7 of this course already taught — no new concepts, just applying them to one real, cumulative scenario.

First, users, groups, and roles. Thirty-five staff who submit requests, four coordinators who triage and assign, and one department head who needs visibility without doing the triage herself. Rather than assigning roles to forty individuals one at a time, build three groups and let role inheritance carry the weight — and make the department head the group manager so she can add or remove her own staff without filing a ticket.

Next, one ACL decision. A custom estimated-cost field needs to stay invisible to staff until a coordinator has reviewed it. A UI Policy alone is client-side only, so it wouldn't stop a report or an integration from exposing the field anyway. The real control is a field-level ACL on that field, requiring the coordinator role for both read and write, enforced at the data layer regardless of how the record is accessed.

Then, one catalog item. Furniture requests are Lakeview's single most common ticket, so instead of letting staff file generic incidents, build a proper Furniture Request catalog item with a small variable set, a catalog UI policy that only requires a current-item field for replacements or relocations, and routing straight to the coordinators group.

Finally, one notification. When a coordinator marks a request Closed Complete, a condition-based notification with an email template tells the requester automatically — no custom event needed, because a simple field-change condition already says exactly what's required here.

Groups and roles, one ACL, one catalog item, one notification — all cumulative, all built on chapters you've already completed. Lesson 36 picks up exactly here: adding form behavior rules, a properties and scheduled-jobs health check, and the Update Set that moves this whole build from Dev to Test to Production.
